content.title: Hear in Hijab

modules.quote: Hear In Hijab is an innovative hearing device that reimagines hearing assistance, integrating sound-enhancing technology into a hijab-compatible design to improve accessibility, safety, and everyday comfort, empowering users to navigate daily life with greater confidence.

content.text: Hearing aids aren't designed for everyone
For millions of Muslim women, the hijab is an essential part of daily life. Yet conventional hearing aids have rarely been designed with hijab wearers in mind.

In Indonesia, where hearing loss affects a significant number of older adults, many women face a difficult compromise between wearing hearing aids comfortably and maintaining the way they choose to wear their hijab. The layers of fabric around the ears can block or distort sound, reducing clarity and increasing everyday safety risks.
As a result, many users are forced to adjust their hijab or accept a less effective hearing experience.

Wardah set out to address an overlooked accessibility challenge by rethinking hearing technology through the lens of cultural inclusion. Rather than adapting existing devices, we sought to create a solution specifically designed for hijab wearers - one that would enhance hearing without requiring users to change their daily routines or personal style.
A device designed for the hijab

Designed to work seamlessly with the hijab, the device captures sound through a microphone positioned outside the hijab, allowing users to receive uninterrupted audio without interference from layers of fabric.

A redesigned hijab pin functions as a sound receiver, discreetly transmitting audio to the user while maintaining comfort and familiarity. By integrating assistive technology into an object already worn every day, Hear In Hijab creates a natural and culturally relevant solution that enhances hearing clarity without compromising personal expression.
The device delivers improved sound amplification of up to 100 dB, helping users better detect important sounds and navigate daily life with greater confidence and safety.
Launched on the International Day of Older Persons, we focused on combining thoughtful design, functionality and inclusivity to empower elderly Muslim women with greater confidence and independence.

More than a product innovation, Hear In Hijab demonstrated how creativity can solve overlooked human challenges - designing technology around people’s lives, cultures and needs to create meaningful impact.

Bonding Instruction

modules.quote: Helping urban families reconnect by turning furniture assembly into a collaborative activity, leveraging themed storytelling visuals and kid-friendly tools to create lasting bonds and memories.

content.text: In today’s fast-paced world, many working parents often struggle to find quality time to balance work, school schedules, and spend meaningful moments with their children. This disconnect makes it challenging for parents and children to bond. Beyond emotional distance, this lack of shared time also puts children’s motor skills and brain development at risk, as they miss out on essential hands-on learning and guided interactions that support their physical and cognitive growth during formative years.

image.alt: Internal double page spread with illustration diagram inside the assembly manual

meta_data.alt: Internal double page spread with illustration diagram inside the assembly manual

content.text: Spending just 20-30 minutes of focus time in shared activities is enough to create a positive memory for personal and emotional development of children. As kids grow, spending less time together makes parents feel more distant. To rebuild this quality time and convert product building time into a bonding time, we designed a revolutionary IKEA instruction manual to make furniture assembly accessible, fun and engaging for parents and children to create together, despite their packed schedules.

image.alt: A family assembling a shelving unit with some fun pirate-theme cartoon illustrations overlaid

meta_data.alt: A family assembling a shelving unit with some fun pirate-theme cartoon illustrations overlaid

content.text: The Bonding Instruction manual incorporated simple yet engaging tweaks to trigger cooperation, filled with step-by-step stories and visuals designed to appeal to children. It features fun stories and visuals in IKEA’s yellow and blue, colors supported by psychological research for promoting calmness, focus, and joyful engagement, helping children’s motor, emotional, and cognitive development. It also comes equipped with a kid friendly hand grip for the Allen key, making it easier for children to take part in the building process.

The campaign utilized both offline and online channels, including in-store displays and interactive Instagram Stories Highlights, to maximize reach and engagement. On International Children’s Day, IKEA launched the campaign, providing the manual book and kid friendly tools with every product purchase related to children’s needs.

IKEA's "Bonding Instruction" campaign effectively turned furniture assembly into a bonding experience, strengthening family connections, supporting the child's growth and development, and enhancing customer affinity.

content.title: ARTISM EXHIBITION

modules.quote: Through Spotify Canvas, we created a new art genre using binaural beats and digital artwork to welcome neurodivergent and autistic people into the art world.

content.text: Approximately 75 million people around the world are on the autism spectrum. Through research, we know that people with the condition have higher theta/beta ratio brainwave frequency in the frontal brain region. This difference has created a stigma around neurodiversity and employment, when often people with autism possess unique creative potential.

For people with autism, Art is more than just a therapy tool that can help with sensory barriers and social skills, for many people art is their life passion, and they aspire to become commercially successful artists.
How can we support neurodiverse people and their creative ambitions?
THE POWER OF BINAURAL BEATS ON BRAINWAVES
Our studies discovered the effects of Binaural Beats on brainwaves. We then worked with Spotify to incorporate specific binaural beats in alpha range into a Spotify playlist.
Artists with autism were then invited to create art whilst listening to the music, supporting their concentration and unlocking their creative potential.

We showcased a new genre of art via Spotify Canvas and enabled everyone to access the resulting "Artism Exhibition" through the Binaural Beats Mix official playlist. To get the attention of Indonesian youth, we worked with the hottest record label in Indonesia and displayed the art at popular music concerts.
We also encouraged people to share the Canvas through social media content, amplifying the digital impact of the exhibition and gaining awareness for this important cause.

content.seo_description: Spotify ARTISM empowers neurodivergent artists using music, binaural beats, and digital art to foster creativity and inclusivity.
content.short_description: An innovative art exhibition where music, art, and neurodiversity intersect to transform lives.

content.text: We are made up of two creative hubs located in New York and Chicago.

Our New York hub is amidst midtown’s electrifying energy. A short walk from Grand Central Station, our office building blends international and modern architecture, marrying the city’s rich history with our dymanic present. Our office space features abundant natural light and a modern approach to desks and meeting rooms. The environment is enriched by displays of our work with pioneering brands including TUMS, Burger King, OREO, 7-Eleven and more.

The Chicago hub was designed by world-renowned Japanese Architect Kenzo Tange—one of the first office spaces to utilize power over ethernet lighting to illuminate using a circadian rhythm for employee wellness. We’re located two blocks west of the Magnificent Mile and two blocks North of the city’s sprawling Riverwalk. For us, Transformative Creativity is what separates distinctive from dime-a-dozen in a beyond noisy world. That’s reflected in the caliber of leading brands we serve: Disney, Intel, The Hershey Company, Famous Footwear, Olive Garden and more. Our office houses a full sound stage with editing suits, so we can create collaboratively and move at the speed of culture. The building also has a state-of-the-art fitness center and an urban outdoor plaza.

content.seo_title: Nutter Butter Case Study | Dentsu Creative
content.seo_description: While some brands follow trends and hijack culture, Nutter Butter created culture through a nutty universe entirely of its own. We built a world where nothing seemed to make sense — by design. The Nutterverse isn’t just a campaign. It's a dimension where the cookie is canon, the fans write the plot, and weird is the strategy. An innovative approach that cemented this cookie into an internet legend.
